# Add direct unit coverage for Neo.util.Date

> **New here? This issue is written to be finishable on a clean clone.** You need Node, a fork and an evening. No Docker, no API key, no AI service, nothing beyond `npm install`. If anything below turns out to need more than that, say so in a comment — that is a bug in the issue, not in you.

## Context

Every date surface in Neo computes its grid through one shared helper, `Neo.util.Date`: the calendar month, week and year views, `Neo.form.field.Date`, `Neo.date.DayViewComponent`, the calendar's event store and its drag plugins.

Measured on 2026-09-19 at `dev@afddc57634`: **no file under `test/playwright/` references `src/util/Date.mjs`** — not by import, not by method name — while more than ten modules under `src/` import it. Its eight static methods are exercised today only as a side effect of rendering a calendar.

## The Problem

Week arithmetic is where off-by-one bugs live: leap years, a month that begins on a Sunday, a `weekStartDay` other than Monday, and the ISO rule that puts the first days of January in the last week of the previous year. Because nothing asserts these methods directly, such a bug first appears as a *wrong calendar*, and whoever fixes it has to reconstruct the failing case from a rendered component before they can even see it.

Direct coverage turns that into a one-line failure with the inputs printed.

## The Architectural Reality

`src/util/Date.mjs` — class `Neo.util.Date` (the local binding is `DateUtil`), extends `Neo.core.Base`. Eight static methods, all pure, none touching the DOM or a worker:

| method | line | contract |
|---|---|---|
| `clone(date)` | `:42` | new `Date` with the same value; `null` in → `null` out |
| `convertToyyyymmdd(date)` | `:51` | `yyyy-mm-dd`, shifted by the local timezone offset first |
| `getDaysInMonth(date)` | `:60` | days in that date's month |
| `getFirstDayOffset(date, weekStartDay)` | `:69` | 0–6, how far the 1st sits from `weekStartDay` |
| `getFirstDayOfMonth(date)` | `:81` | weekday of the 1st, 0–6 (Sun–Sat) |
| `getWeekOfYear(targetDate)` | `:91` | ISO 8601 week number, computed in UTC |
| `getWeeksOfMonth(date, weekStartDay)` | `:112` | documented as 5 or 6 |
| `matchDate(date1, date2)` | `:125` | same day, month and year |

## The Fix

Add one new spec: **`test/playwright/unit/util/Date.spec.mjs`**.

Copy the shape from its sibling `test/playwright/unit/util/String.spec.mjs` — the first eleven lines matter and are not optional:

```javascript
import {setup} from '../../setup.mjs';

setup({
    appConfig: {
        name: 'DateUtilTest'
    }
});

import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import Neo            from '../../../../src/Neo.mjs';
import * as core      from '../../../../src/core/_export.mjs';
import DateUtil       from '../../../../src/util/Date.mjs';

test.describe('Neo.util.Date', () => {
    // your tests
});
```

`setup()` must be called before the other imports; that is how the Neo class system is initialised for the unit tier.

**Cases worth asserting** — pick the ones you can state confidently; you do not have to cover all eight methods to have a useful PR:

- `clone()` returns a *different* object with an equal value, and passes `null` through.
- `getDaysInMonth()` across February 2024 (29) and February 2023 (28).
- `getFirstDayOfMonth()` and `getFirstDayOffset()` for a month starting on a Sunday, with `weekStartDay: 0` and with `weekStartDay: 1` — the offset is documented as 0–6 and the wrap is the interesting half.
- `getWeekOfYear()` on the ISO boundary: 2021-01-01 (a Friday) and 2019-12-30 (a Monday) are the classic pair where the calendar year and the ISO week year disagree.
- `matchDate()` for two `Date` objects on the same day at different times.
- `getWeeksOfMonth()` is documented as returning 5 or 6. February of a non-leap year that begins exactly on `weekStartDay` is 28 days in exactly four rows. **Assert what the function actually returns for that input and say so in your PR** — if it is not 4, that is worth knowing, and it is a finding rather than something for you to fix here.

Deterministic inputs only: construct explicit `new Date(2024, 1, 1)` values. No `new Date()`, no "today" — a test that depends on the day it runs will fail for someone else.

## How to run it

```bash
npm install
npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/util/Date.spec.mjs
```

The whole unit tier is `npm run test-unit`. **Do not run a bare `npx playwright test`** — this repository has several Playwright configurations and the default one is not the unit tier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/util/Date.spec.mjs` exists and follows the `setup()`-first shape of its sibling specs.
- [ ] At least four of the eight methods are asserted, each with inputs written out literally — no dependency on the current date, the machine's locale, or test execution order.
- [ ] The spec passes on the unit configuration, and the PR body says how you ran it.
- [ ] The `getWeeksOfMonth` four-row case is either asserted or reported in the PR body with the value it returned.
- [ ] No file outside `test/playwright/unit/util/` is changed. If a test of yours goes red against `src/util/Date.mjs`, do not fix the source here — say so in the PR and we will open a separate issue for the fix, with your test as its evidence.

## Out of Scope

- Changing anything in `src/util/Date.mjs`. This issue adds coverage to the code as it stands.
- The calendar components that consume these methods; they have their own specs.
- Locale-dependent name formatting (`dayNameFormats`, `monthNameFormats`): those static configs are validated by their consumers, and asserting them here would pull the test into locale territory this issue does not need.

## Before you open the PR

- Branch from `dev` and target `dev` — not `main`.
- Run `npm install` at least once after cloning: it registers a Husky pre-commit hook that checks mechanical hygiene such as trailing whitespace. Committing without it will fail CI on something unrelated to your test.
- <https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md> has the rest.
